items.title: Junior Mance Part I interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, New York City, New York, July 27, 1995…
items.q: It’s going to be two CDs featuring like three albums, “Cannonball’s Sharp Shooters,” and Nat’s album “To The Ivy League” and there was one more “Cannonball En Route” I think is the name of it.

ctx.x: First of all I got to say if I had to pick a quintet that just to me had a beautiful jazz feeling and a beautiful soul feeling it would be the Cannonball quintet.

You know, strange you mention that because this last week, Verve Records called me and sent me two cassettes they’re going to re-issue. They bought the catalogue I think, the old catalogue from Mercury on those sides that we did that you’re talking about and they’re going to put them out in a double CD. And they sent them to me to listen to and clarify like some of the, there were a lot of errors as far as composer credits, and that’s why they sent them to me along with the sheet with the thing on it, which I had…

you could put your civilian clothes on, on any Army post in the States (not overseas). But I’m sitting there, you know I’m walking guard duty with combat boots, helmet, cartridge belt, and so Cannonball’s giving me like such a look of disdain, I’ve never seen in my life, like wow, who is this cat? And the rest of the guys in the band are looking like, “Huh?” So Cannonball asked, he says, “What do you want to play?” I says, “Well play anything out of your book.” And by saying it like that, you know, that kind of…

items.title: Junior Mance Part II interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 18, 1999 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: No, this is with Cannonball and Nat. The tune is called “Spectacular.”

ctx.x: Is that — that’s not from that jam session album with Dinah Washington?
No, this is with Cannonball and Nat. The tune is called “Spectacular.”
[scats] “Spectacular” right, yeah. Jimmy Cobb on drums and Sam Jones. You know when that was? 1956. Forty something years, forty two years ago.
